what_this_is: A raw JSON-RPC 2.0 exchange with the ingredient-db MCP server over stdio, captured by eval/capture_wire.py with no MCP library on the client side. Each `raw` field is the line exactly as it crossed the pipe (verbatim copy: out/wire_raw.jsonl). Each `annotations` field is written by hand, one entry per top-level field of that message.
where_the_model_call_happens: The model call (Gemini, via rag/llm.py call_with_tools) happens only in the HOST process (rag/mcp_host.py -> rag/agent.py). It never happens in the ingredient-db server, which only receives a tool name and arguments over stdin and answers with JSON, and none of the 9 messages below carries a prompt, a model name or an API key.

annotations.jsonrpc: Protocol tag. Always the string "2.0"; MCP is JSON-RPC 2.0, nothing custom.
annotations.id: 1. Chosen by the HOST. The reply must echo it, which is how a reply is matched to its request on a pipe that carries many messages.
annotations.method: "initialize": the handshake. Must be the first request on a new connection; no tool can be listed or called before it.
annotations.params: What the host offers. protocolVersion = the spec revision the host speaks (2025-11-25). capabilities = features the HOST supports for the server to use (sampling, roots, elicitation); empty here, so this server can never ask our side to run a model. clientInfo = the host's self-reported name/version, unauthenticated.

annotations.id: 1. Same id as the request, so this is the answer to message 1.
annotations.result: Present instead of `error` because the handshake succeeded. protocolVersion = the version the server agrees to (it may downgrade; the host must accept or disconnect). capabilities = what the SERVER offers: tools, resources, prompts, each with listChanged=false (the list is fixed for the whole session, so the host does not need to watch for changes). serverInfo = the server's self-reported name and version. Note that "version" is 1.30.0, the MCP SDK's version, not a release number the content team assigned, so it cannot be used to pin or verify which build of the server we are running.

annotations.method: "notifications/initialized": the host confirms it has accepted the server's answer and normal traffic can start.
annotations.(no id): A message with NO id is a notification. The server must not reply, and it does not; there is no server -> host line for this step.

annotations.method: "tools/list": DISCOVERY. The host asks which tools exist instead of having them hard-coded. rag/mcp_host.py sends exactly this once per server at start-up.
annotations.(no params): Omitted. It could carry a pagination `cursor`; this server returns everything in one page.

tools.name: lookup_ingredient
tools.description:
Search the ingredient database by name and return candidate records
(id, canonical name, aliases). Use the returned id or name with
get_allergens or get_nutrition_per_100g.

tools.name: get_allergens
tools.description:
Return the EU-14 allergen flags for one ingredient: `contains` (present
by recipe) and `may_contain` (cross-contact risk declared by the supplier).
An empty `contains` list with a non-empty `may_contain` is NOT allergen-free.

tools.name: get_nutrition_per_100g
tools.description:
Return nutrition per 100 g for one ingredient: kcal, protein, fat,
carbohydrate, sugars, fibre and salt, all in grams except kcal.

annotations.result: result.tools = the 3 tools this server exposes. Per tool: name = what the model will call; description = the Python DOCSTRING, which is the text the model reads when choosing a tool (so it is a prompt); inputSchema = JSON Schema generated from the type hints, which the host forwards to Gemini unchanged as parameters_json_schema; outputSchema = the shape of structuredContent in results. The allergen legend is NOT here: it is a resource (resources/list), which the host attaches itself instead of letting the model fetch it each turn. No nextCursor, so this is the complete list.

annotations.method: "tools/call": run one tool. In the live agent the host sends this only after the MODEL, running in the host process, has replied with a function call. The server never learns that a model was involved.
annotations.params: name = the tool (get_allergens). arguments = the JSON object the model produced, validated by the server against inputSchema. This string (the user's ingredient) is exactly what the third-party server sees and writes to its query log.

annotations.result: content = a list of content blocks; here one text block holding the JSON as a string, which is what rag/mcp_host.py parses and hands to the model. structuredContent = the same data as a real JSON object, matching outputSchema, for hosts that validate. isError=false: the tool ran and found the ingredient (milk).

annotations.params: Same tool, an ingredient the database does not have (the brief's own example).

content.text: Error executing tool get_allergens: no ingredient matched 'creme fraiche lite'. Try: 'creme-fraiche'.

annotations.result: Still a `result`, NOT a JSON-RPC `error`. The PROTOCOL call succeeded; the TOOL failed. isError=true tells the host this is a tool failure, and content carries the message the model will read: "no ingredient matched ... Try: 'creme-fraiche'". That is a RECOVERABLE error: it names the miss and the next move. A JSON-RPC `error` object (code -32601 etc.) is reserved for protocol faults like an unknown method, and hosts usually do not show those to the model at all.
